**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Mostly green, flat leaf with very fine, uniformly distributed stippling/tiny dark dots across the entire surface. No large lesions, no yellowing, no powdery coating, no curling.

- **Ruled out**: Early/Late Blight (large necrotic lesions), Bacterial/Septoria Spot (distinct circular spots with borders/halos), Powdery Mildew (white powder), Leaf Mold (pale patches), Mosaic/Tomato Mosaic Virus (mottled dark/light green along veins), TYLCV (leaf curling + yellowing), Verticillium Wilt (V-shaped necrosis + yellowing), Target Spot (distinct concentric ring lesions).

- **Best match — Spider Mites**: The uniform fine stippling across a still-green leaf is the hallmark of early spider mite feeding damage, where individual cell punctures create a granular/sandpaper texture. The Spider Mites reference images (bottom-right quadrant) show nearly identical green leaves with this fine stippling pattern before major yellowing develops.
